id: transcript::2025-08-03_scd2mK_eSro_The Easiest Upsells::0000
text: The easiest upsells in the world is that you can sell more of what you just offered them. You can sell better of what you just offered them. You can also sell new or different, something that's complimentary. So, you can sell fries with a Coke. You can sell a burger and then add in fries or add in a Coke. And then each of those you can upsize. You can superers size them. That's more. And then if you had a better version of Coke, you say, "Well, do you want organic Coke?" Just get creative and think, "What else do this person want?" And one of the easiest things to do is just ask them, "What else can I do to make this easier for you?" And then sell that.

id: transcript::2025-08-06_NzXZqWuaPWs_Sales Close That Works With Anything::0000
text: One of the big things that I like to train with our team is something that I call all-purpose closes. So, these are closes that uh pretty much work in all situations. And all-purpose closes might sound like they're like, "I think it's a lot of money." And say, "Do you think the fact that you haven't invested in the past is the reason that you're not successful? Do you feel like the fact that you struggled to make decisions in the past is why you're on the phone with me today?" Like, you just take their objection and add, "Do you think that's the reason that you haven't succeeded?" Because they haven't succeeded yet. That's the thing that you have to your advantage. They're on the phone. They have the pain.

id: transcript::2025-08-06_Qn5Ea9BvT_M_How To Improve A Sales Team::0000
text: If you have somebody on your sales team or you're the person on your sales team who sells way more than everybody else, here's the way to get that person to help everybody else. Instead of asking them, "Hey, what are you doing different?" ignore what they say. Cuz most people are very bad at teaching. Instead, watch the game footage. Watch them actually do the sales process and figure out what are the differences in terms of how they set things up, how they introduce price, and how they close. Usually, those are the three big points. basically how they're introducing the call, how they're introducing the offer, and then ultimately how they close, the price, and the transaction are kind of the three points of greatest leverage in the conversation. And sometimes you can take the little things that that person says and put it into every script so that everyone becomes just like the top closer.

id: transcript::2025-08-10_B4CBmyby_a0_How I Learned To Advertise::0000
text: I got on a phone with a bunch of agencies and they were like $3 to $5,000 a month and I could not afford that for at all. I knew how to run ads at the time, but I needed to get better, right? And so finally, it was like the third or fourth call. I was like, "Hey man, like what would it take?" That's the magic question. What would it take for you to teach me oneonone? He's like, "I don't sell my time." And I said, "Okay, it's America. Just give me a price that you think you would do it for." And he said, "Uh, 750 an hour." And I was like, "Deal?" He ended up doing once a week with me for an hour. And so for the first few weeks, the deal was I'm the only one who touched the computer. So, you show me what you're doing, but I'm gonna I'm gonna do it. So, you can tell me where I'm messing up if I get stuck. And then after the sixth call that I did, I was like, I don't need this guy. I did two more calls. I didn't have anything that that came up. And so, for $6,000, basically the cost of one month of running this agency, I was able to learn the skill from one of the best agency owners. And then I used that skill for like the rest of my advertising career.
source: 2025-08-10_B4CBmyby_a0_How I Learned To Advertise
title: How I Learned To Advertise

source: 2025-08-12_PFYwEaDojeA_Why The First 48 Hours Are So Important

id: transcript::2025-08-14_xXKiIFbO95Y_Almost No One Lives To 100::0000
text: Three out of 10,000 people live to 100. Everyone has this assumption in their mind that they're like, "Yeah, I'm at 50, so I'm going to make it to 100." Yeah. Well, you've got a three in 10,000 shot at doing that. Very unlikely. More realistically, you'll die at the median, which is 74 for men in the US, which means that at 37, you're actually at the halfway point, just in years. But if you adjust for the increase in speed of time, so the same reason that your kid at 5 years old thinks that something takes forever when you say it's going to happen next year, and when you're 40, something that happens next year feels like you blink your eyes and it's there, is that when you're five, 1 year is 20% of your life. When you're 40, 1 year is 2 1/2% of your life. And so it very much in real way is 9 times faster than it is for your 5-year-old. And so if you adjust for that time speed, your midpoint isn't 37.
source: 2025-08-14_xXKiIFbO95Y_Almost No One Lives To 100
title: Almost No One Lives To 100

id: transcript::2025-08-30_hxO9evVdZwQ_7 Lessons I Learned The Hard Way::0000
text: I sold my last company for $46.2 million. Here are seven lessons I learned the hard way. One, nobody knows you exist. Advertise more. Number two, be willing to repeat yourself. People need to be reminded more than need to be taught. Three, the proof you get from happy customers is way more convincing than any promise you can make in marketing. So, get testimonials and use them often. Four, raising prices almost always makes you more money. But you hear no more often, and that's okay. id: transcript::2025-09-01_r0RykaUNHUE_How To Find Better Customers::0000
text: This is for everybody. I do this with honestly more than half the businesses that I buy and it's one of the biggest value unlocks you can possibly do in your business. Look at all the customers that you have sold. Look at the ones that are the top 20% or the top 10% that have done really well. Then look at all of them and say, "What do all these people have in common?" And specifically, what do they have or not have that everybody else has or doesn't have? And the idea is that you want to select one, two, three, maybe four characteristics that make them unique. Do you think demographics? What do they look like? Who are these people? Think psychoraphics, what are the things they believe? You think geographics, where do they live? You think activities, what have they done or what did they do that other people didn't do? And when you put those things together, you'll be able to get really laser targeted on the type of customer that you provide the most value to. That's the formal way of doing it. The back of napkin way of doing it is think about the clients you love. Think about what those people have in common, the ones that you help the most. Just find those and be willing to say no to people who aren't
source: 2025-09-01_r0RykaUNHUE_How To Find Better Customers
title: How To Find Better Customers

id: transcript::2025-09-04_k2llX3TAucU_How Restaurants Use Mints To Make More Money::0000
text: Here's how a restaurant uses mints to make more money and how you can use the same psychology in your business to make more. So, what they did is they took the bowl of mints instead of leaving it by the door, they gave it to the waitresses to hand out. The first thing they did was just give people one mint. And when they gave people one mint, they got an average of 3% increase in tips. When they gave people two mints, they got a 14% increase in tips. But in the third style, where they gave a mint to one person, then walked away and then came back and then gave them a second, they got a 23% increase in tips. And so there's three things that make this so powerful. Number one, you give a gift to somebody, people want to give you something back. Second is that it was most powerful in the third scenario because it was personalized. They're like, "Wait a second, I'm actually going to give you a second one." And the third it was unexpected.
source: 2025-09-04_k2llX3TAucU_How Restaurants Use Mints To Make More Money

id: transcript::2025-09-08_wQj-KN9-YgE_The 5 Stages Of Entrepreneurship::0000
text: There's five stages that most newer entrepreneurs or people who want to pursue income go through. So the first is uninformed optimism. So your friend tells you about this thing they made 10 grand on and you're like that sounds amazing. You're uninformed but you're optimistic, right? And then all of a sudden you get to informed pessimism. So you get in and then you put your money in and then it drops and you're like wow this sucks. And then you know people are like buy the dip. And so you're like okay I'm going to I'm going to put more money in. And so then you get to kind of stage three which is the value of despair where you're like oh my god I've lost so much money. I have no idea what's what's going on right now. And at stage three, there's kind of a fork. And so either people then go, "Well, my other friend told me about this other thing." And they jump back to step one. And then they just funnel through that loop over and over again. To break through that that dip, you have to basically get to stage four, which is informed optimism. Now you understand the rules of the game. You understand the variables at play. And it's not as good as you thought it was, but you at least get it. And so from there then you can get to achievement.
source: 2025-09-08_wQj-KN9-YgE_The 5 Stages Of Entrepreneurship
title: The 5 Stages Of Entrepreneurship

id: transcript::2025-09-10_KEr-Sa3uBZM_The Best Way To Learn Sales::0000
text: If you're new to sales, you want to be a trash man. Let me explain. In companies that we have, we like to do something called lead scoring. id: transcript::2025-09-17_dTdQhvZ9VEI_Is It Worth Changing::0000
text: In any given function, let's say that this is your baseline of performance. Now, whenever you change anything, in my experience, you get about a 20% decrease in performance immediately. id: transcript::2025-09-20_6f2HAr91mPE_A Lesson From My First Job Ever::0000
text: My first job ever was being a blender tender at Smoothie King. And so one day I asked the owner, "Hey, why is it when you know something's damaged or something's expired, we can't just have it, right? Like we can't sell it, so why can't we just keep it?" He said, "You want to know why?" He said, "Because all of a sudden, if you guys can have it," he said, "we're going to have way more expired and way more broken bags that are going to start happening." I was like, "Oh." The lesson that I learned from that is we have to be careful about the incentives, especially the ones that we don't even think about. The question is is like what is that broken bag of chips in your business and is there a way that sometimes it's worth taking the small cost today to avoid the big cultural risk
source: 2025-09-20_6f2HAr91mPE_A Lesson From My First Job Ever

id: transcript::2025-09-20_Grs3IB6GrWM_I Always Start For Free::0000
text: Every single business to this day, I still start with free stuff because I want to get feedback from people. I want to know what they liked, what they didn't like, what their pain points are. I want to figure out how to how to smooth out the process. I want to figure out all these different things. And me trying to guess at that on my first shot and ask people to pay me, I'm like, I don't want to do that. I'm going to have a bad reputation. I don't want it.
source: 2025-09-20_Grs3IB6GrWM_I Always Start For Free
title: I Always Start For Free

id: transcript::2025-09-26_pFvjKjOxXcw_4 Ways To Buy Stuff::0000
text: There's four different ways you can buy stuff, right? First off is you can take on debt. So you can take other people's money. That's the first way you can buy something. The second way is you can save up for it, right? Your savings. The third is that you have cash flow. So that's your current income or money that's coming in from the work you do. The fourth way that you can buy it is what I call new money. Now, this one I think is the most important because it's the one that most people should probably use. Don't go into debt to buy stuff you shouldn't buy. If you save, I don't think it's a terrible idea, but if it's going to buy, let's say you want to buy a sick ass house or a sick car or something like that, sometimes you want to do that because you're going to die eventually and maybe you do want to spend some money. Fine. Well, I'd rather do it off cash flow than savings. But is there something better than cash flow? Yeah, let me do a special project so that I can buy a special item. That way I can continue to hit all my goals in a very clear way while still having
source: 2025-09-26_pFvjKjOxXcw_4 Ways To Buy Stuff
title: 4 Ways To Buy Stuff

id: transcript::2025-09-27_5jGFq7nYO-g_You Dont Need More Views::0000
text: I have two businesses that I looked at in the last year that were doing over a million dollars a year with less than 5,000 followers. You absolutely can make plenty of money with a very small following as long as you make content that's directly valuable for that following. If you're making stuff about how to fix pianos because you're a piano repair guy, you might be like, man, I'm only getting, you know, a,000 views a video. It's like, yeah, but the market of people who are buying pianos might be significantly smaller than the market of people who just want to be entertained or distracted, right? If I were to think to myself like I have a room of a thousand people that are going to watch this and all of them are only interested in fixing pianos, that's a hell of an opportunity.
source: 2025-09-27_5jGFq7nYO-g_You Dont Need More Views
title: You Don't Need More Views

text: Paul Graham said this quote on Twitter the other day and I really liked it. He said, "If you want to make a million dollars, you must endure a million dollars of pain. id: transcript::2025-10-06_NM2sRGKunkE_You Have To Win Alone::0000
text: People only root for people who don't need it. The amount of times when I was on my lonely path where I was too different from the friends that I had but not successful enough to be friends with the people that I wanted to be friends with. That's when that's when you want people to root for you. That's when you want people to support you. Once you've already won, people are like, "He's amazing. He's so good." But like that's the time when you need it the least. You always have to be the person who roots for you before everybody else does. And it's usually a single clap in the auditorium for a very long period of time. It is a slow clap that's just you rooting for you. People struggle to do things alone. And the path of the exceptional person is one of an exception which means that you are not with other people. And rather than fighting that or bemoning it, see it as an indicator that you're on the right path. Because if everyone else were cheering you on, then it means you're not in the right place. Because it means you're just like everyone else. And that's not where you want to be.
source: 2025-10-06_NM2sRGKunkE_You Have To Win Alone
title: You Have To Win Alone

id: transcript::2025-10-06_lx7cLSg9JoA_I Think You Can Do More::0000
text: I had a conversation the other day with somebody who reports into me and I said, "Hey, I don't think I've seen nearly the production from you as I expected. I think it's less than you're capable of. Would you agree?" That way it's not an insult. I'm saying like, "I just think you're doing less than I think your your potential is." And he was like, "Yeah, I would agree." And I said, "Okay, do you think it's because there's only five reasons? So, did you know not know that I wanted you to do this thing? Did you not know what I wanted you to do? Did you not know how to do it? Were you not motivated to do it? Or did you have something that was getting in your way?" He was like, "Well, there's something else that's blocking me." I was like, "Well, tell me what's blocking you." And he said, "Well, these are the things that I had to do this week." I said, "How long has this taken you?" He said, "Three weeks." And I said, "Do you think you can do more than that?" He said, "Yes." And I said, "Great. Here's a bunch more stuff that you can do. Get it done by tomorrow." And then he got it done by that night. He heard it loud and clear, but I wasn't like, "You suck. You're lazy." I was like, I expect more of you because I think you're really capable.
source: 2025-10-06_lx7cLSg9JoA_I Think You Can Do More
title: I Think You Can Do More

id: transcript::2025-10-07_mfry-2BS1fw_Sell To Better Customers::0000
text: If you increase the quality of your prospects, you will increase the quality of your product. At Gym Launch, we figured out that gym owners that were the most successful had three things in common, assigned lease, they had at least one employee, they had at least 30 customers. So, if someone has all three of those things, they'll make a ton of money with our thing. We told the sales team then, we said, "If they don't have these three things, do not sell them." We told the marketing team, "Say this in all of our marketing. If they don't have these three things, tell them this is not for them." So, what happened? We sold better people. Guess what happened after that? Our average results went up. Guess what we could do after that? Market average better results. And what do we do? Get better customers. And so it becomes a virtuous cycle that improves the product. Here's the crazy part. We didn't actually change anything about what we sold.
source: 2025-10-07_mfry-2BS1fw_Sell To Better Customers
title: Sell To Better Customers

id: transcript::2025-10-08_Ew8El6shC2o_The ONE Thing..::0000
text: What is the single principle of business you wish every entrepreneur understood before they start? >> The one thing I think if I had to really boil it down to one, it'd be volume. The amount of volume and repetition that is required to excel in any domain is typically not twice as much or 10 times as much. It's usually in the order of magnites of thousands of times as much work and repetition as you think it is. I think that is the fundamental discrepancy that causes people to fail is that they thought that I post one time or I'll post 10 times and all of a sudden I will become famous or I will get viral or my marketing will work on my 10th ad or my 10th door knock, my 10th email that I do outreach on that the more experienced guys are like, "Okay, how do I send 10,000 emails a day and do that for 10 years?" It's hard to fathom when you're starting out that someone can actually do 10,000 times more than you. But the people who are 10,000 times ahead of you, because there are people 10,000 times richer than people who are starting out, probably did 10,000 times the repetition. And so if you can do volume, lots of volume with tremendous leverage, then you get huge output.
source: 2025-10-08_Ew8El6shC2o_The ONE Thing..
title: The ONE Thing..

text: How do you and Ila balance love, marriage, and empire? What are the non-negotiables that keep your relationship thriving at such high stakes? >> I think we balance it by not focusing on balancing like not judging how we are doing in this season. So if we have more business in one season and we have more relationship in another, it's just seasons. It's just life. And I think if one of us feels like a need or a huge discrepancy, then we just say it like, "Hey, let's do a date night or something." Or, "Hey, let's let's take some time just us and we'll do that." But even at that date night, it's like, well, do you do you not talk about business? It's like what what would I talk about? Like what did you do today? Don't tell me, you know, like it's like we're we're both why would we not talk about something we both care about. I think that there's difference between talking about business, like the fun part of business, which I would say we focus on, which is like what's the future look like? What are the things we're excited about versus like what's the HR complaint of the day? And so I think if you're like talking about problems, I think that's probably just not going to be fun no matter what you're doing. source: 2025-10-09_L8pw-8Us_oE_How We Balance Relationship And Business

id: transcript::2025-10-14_P3Ylz3PkmPw_Youre Going To Look Stupid::0000
text: You're going to look stupid. You're going to have to learn how to try significantly harder and longer than you expected. id: transcript::2025-10-14_RB_I78KLPEM_4 Lessons From The Rock::0000
text: Yes, I am huge, but not as huge as The Rock's net worth. Here are four things I learned from The Rock. Number one, he's been in this for 27 years. And so to compare my brand or someone else's brand to somebody who's been doing this for almost three decades, hey, you look great for your age, by the way, is crazy. Don't compare your first year to someone's 30th. Number two, work ethic. One of the things he's been known for is he shows up on the set first. He's last to leave. He never skips his workouts. He brings the gym with him because he always wants to put the extra reps in. Not natural talent. Work ethic. Number three, expanding the niche. He started as a football player and then he became a WWE wrestler and then he got into action films as a low man on the boat and then he became able to star in action films and now he's in Disney movies that are broad. He has continued to lean into growth and expansion for who he is and what he represents. And number four, he tastefully monetized his brand by doing things that people already loves him for. They already know that he works out, so he has a pre-workout supplement, energy drink, and they know that he stays out late, so the energy drink makes sense. He likes apparel, so his Project Rock with Under Armour made sense. Now, if he came out and started selling Lamborghinis, it probably wouldn't make sense with his brand.
source: 2025-10-14_RB_I78KLPEM_4 Lessons From The Rock
title: 4 Lessons From The Rock

id: transcript::2025-10-14_vexpVwNjqP4_How To Properly Get A Raise::0000
text: You have to figure out how your job directly ties to revenue in the business. And if you don't know, ask. And then once you understand how you directly tie to money, then drive towards that. Every position in the business makes the business more money. Even if you're like, I'm a frontline customer service rep. It's like, okay, well, how do you like if I had to ask that person like how do you make the business money? The answer is if I do a good job, people will come back and buy again. If I do a good job, we'll have a lower percentage of people who will refund. If I do a good job, the business will be able to command higher prices off of word of mouth in the future. Well, then if those are the things that drive revenue, then I'm going to try and focus on those things. And then you can ask your boss and this is a great question is what would it take for me to make this? It's not saying I need to make that. It's just asking them to solve the problem. Like what would it take for me to earn that? And then they can give you an objective metric. Now your boss might not be high enough. And then you say cool can you ask the person above you? By doing it that way you're also being clear like I want to make the business more money and in doing so I would like a small percentage of the increase that I'm able to bring. What would it take?
source: 2025-10-14_vexpVwNjqP4_How To Properly Get A Raise
title: How To Properly Get A Raise

id: transcript::2025-10-15_eaS8QB3-H_U_Why People Dont Want To Work For You::0000
text: What is limiting most of y'all's businesses, which is the stuff that no one actually wants to talk about, is the fact that like you aren't good enough as entrepreneurs. So, you haven't achieved enough yet. You haven't sustained the success you have long enough. And people don't want to work for you because they don't believe in the vision you have. That's the real thing. Because business at the highest level can really be boiled down to find world-class people and get out of their way. You've heard Branson talk about it. You've heard Steve Jobs talk about it. And it's true. The problem is they don't want to work for you. Real. Because Steve Jobs is like, "We're going to add another hundred billion to Apple." And people were like, "Wow, that sounds amazing." And when you meet world-class talent like that, those guys are making $20 million bonuses per year, right? Different levels to the game. And so I bring this up to say that if you are a small business, which is the vast majority of people here, then you have to win on character. They have to want to work for you.

id: transcript::2025-10-16_HyoGTQAzNlM_5 Things Taylor Swift Does Well::0000
text: Terara Swift became a billionaire this year and entered the Forbes list for self-made women in America. Here's five things I've learned about her personal brand that I used to build mine. Number one, you may not know this, but she's been doing this for almost 20 years. She's published her first song when she was 16 years old. She's 33 today. She's got 17 years under her belt. The second thing, scaling the unscalable. She does these public acts where she shows up at someone's wedding, which you could never do to every single fan, but she does it for one, so then it can scale to everyone else and they can imagine that fairy tale for themselves. Number three is that she shows vulnerability. She writes songs about the darkest parts of her life, not about the highlight reel. Number four is ownership. Rather than always sell away the rights, she owns them that she can have control and more flexibility. And ultimately, I think is one of the key reasons she's been able to build her empire the way it is. And number five, she's embraced that she's willing to change. The reason her tour was called Arrows is because she's gone through different eras of her career and she was able to connect with girls from 13 years old all the way to women in their 50s and 60s because they can all relate to the eras of growth we all go throat.
source: 2025-10-16_HyoGTQAzNlM_5 Things Taylor Swift Does Well
title: 5 Things Taylor Swift Does Well

id: transcript::2025-10-18_3Lq-7OeygZw_Kylie Jenner Billionaire Lessons::0000
text: Kylie Jenner became a billionaire at age 21. And here's what I learned from how she did it. So, number one is that she started having a personal brand. She was 5 years old. And so, even though people see her quote overnight success at age 20, she was actually 15 years into the game at that point. She already had a decade plus under her belt and now has two decades. Number two is that the things that she picked were strategic. She used things that had high leverage in terms of her products. She wasn't selling tax services. She was selling direct to consumer products that could be multiplied at scale. She outsourced her weaknesses. And so she partnered with people who'd already had 10, 20 years of experience in logistics, in building sites, in formulating and manufacturing products. She didn't learn that stuff. She found people who did. She embraces controversy. So when controversies come up, rather than shying away, she controls the narrative. It's something that the entire Kardashian family does amazingly well. She's also adaptable based on media platforms. She started in traditional television, has transitioned to Hulu, and embraced new social media platforms as they came out. And finally, she is accessible. She does videos without having all the makeup on. She's more relatable, which is an even bigger achievement because of her superstardom in Americana royalty.
source: 2025-10-18_3Lq-7OeygZw_Kylie Jenner Billionaire Lessons

id: transcript::2025-10-21_jjwXgFTOVho_What Actually Matters Once We Die::0000
text: As someone who recently wrote a eulogy about this, I find it interesting when I think about what things we use to describe other human beings at the end of their life to summarize everything that happened. And what's very interesting to me is that the accomplishments that the person goes through is about one to two sentences. No one cares. Even though it's something that we dedicate a huge amount of our time to, what I did find that was interesting is that there was two things that persistently come up as the things that people talk about. Number one, service and number two, character. It's how did they behave and what did they do as a result of this this idealistic behavior. Like at my funeral, no one will give a about how many books I sold. No one will care about the business that we built. No one ever the houses, the real estate, the the the equity. And like no one will care. No one will care. At the end of your life, the only thing that people will talk about is how you helped other people and how you behaved.
source: 2025-10-21_jjwXgFTOVho_What Actually Matters Once We Die
title: What Actually Matters Once We Die?

id: transcript::2025-10-22_44x4d2UkOBw_Would They Want You To Suffer::0000
text: No one wants to think, man, my parent died. How do I get better from this? Like, it feels like an almost uncomfortable thought. But if you think about your parent dying or your dog dying or you getting broken up with or whatever the bad thing that happened to you, what other frame serves you? And do you think that that person that let you down would want you to be worse off? No. I know for me, for sure not right. That person would want me to be better from it. They wouldn't want me to be permanently traumatized. They wouldn't want me to be permanently changing my behavior in a way that is antithetical to my goals, against my goals, makes it less likely that I get what I want out of life. Why would they want that for me? Why would they want that for you? Right? And so I think one of the things that's very important for like that I also had to break, you know, in thinking through this is that how long I mourn has nothing to do with how much I loved. Period.
source: 2025-10-22_44x4d2UkOBw_Would They Want You To Suffer
title: Would They Want You To Suffer?

id: transcript::2025-10-24_ctC9n_eR5lA_7 Income Streams Is BS::0000
text: Having seven income streams to become a millionaire is BS. And I'm going to show you why in 60 seconds. So let's say this is you and this is your time and attention that you have to pursue any new opportunity. So you say, I need seven income streams because the average millionaire has seven income streams. So I'm going to spread myself thin between seven different opportunities. And I'm going to wait until one of these things takes off. But the reality is it's not which of these ones will work. Any of them could work if you put the work in. It's absolutely true that people who are the wealthiest have multiple income streams. But what's not true is about how they got there. The wealthiest people in the world go all in on one income stream and they keep adding it up over and over and over again until it overflows. They then start diversifying back between the other different ways. But they made their wealth focusing on one thing and then they maintain their wealth by distributing it. You don't make money by splitting your attention up. You make it by focusing on the one thing that matters
source: 2025-10-24_ctC9n_eR5lA_7 Income Streams Is BS
title: 7 Income Streams Is BS

id: transcript::2025-10-25_SWhO6k3qvmY_5 Years Is What It Takes::0000

id: transcript::2025-11-21_qwrEwrPf7I8_Make Failure Unreasonable::0000
text: Volume negates luck. You have to do so much work, so many repetitions that it would be unreasonable to not be successful. And if you think about actually putting that number down and saying, "If I did this 100 times, I did this a thousand times, it would be unreasonable that this doesn't work." Then all you have to do is just do it after that. And the crazy thing is that the bar for success has never been lowered because so few people will try anything at all. And the few people who do try give up quickly. And if they even do try consistently, they don't do it with enough cadence that they do it with too long of intervals in between. So they're not consistent. And so it's like if you can just do something consistently, you beat everyone. But this has always been since the dawn of time the only way to win at everything. And so like if you can't be consistent with something, figure that out cuz nothing's going to work.

id: transcript::2025-11-22_G8byKRANK3Y_Do You Have A Job Or A Business::0000
text: So most business owners think that they own a business when in reality they own a very expensive high-paying job. Investors don't buy businesses that can't survive without the founder. So it doesn't matter how much revenue you do. If every decision, you know, comes from you, every client, and every fire comes back to you, the value of the business is close to zero. And it's something that we call human risk. And so until you solve it, you don't have an asset. You achieve a liability.

id: transcript::2025-11-24_-J0DqskLdoU_The Goal Of Good Branding::0000
text: So what is brand? Right? Brand is the association we make between two things through an outcome. Fundamentally, it's teaching at scale. So this is a tree and if I say tree to a kid over and over again, they will associate the sound with that thing. And so then eventually they will say, "Oh, that is a tree." And so branding will have occurred, right? It's teaching. And so you have your existing brand and then you have the new association that you want and we have some people that may get left behind and say, "I don't like this new association." And then you will have some people that you will gain as a result of the new association. This would be an even trade. The ideal branding move would be like this. We lose this, we gain this. And so whenever you change a brand from anything, you will always lose some and net others because any change will get some people to say no and other people to say yes. And the goal of good branding is that we net more than we lose.
source: 2025-11-24_-J0DqskLdoU_The Goal Of Good Branding
title: The Goal Of Good Branding

id: transcript::2025-11-24_lkWIdDdc3uc_5 Things To Get People To Buy::0000
text: And as somebody who has trained many, many, [music] many salespeople, this is the simplest structure for getting [music] people to consistently speak in a way that gets people to buy. These are the five things that you need to look for. [music] Number one is that you have to speak loud enough that they can hear you. This should sound obvious. The [music] second part of sales tone is that you have to speak slowly enough that they can comprehend you. The third is that you have to articulate what you're saying so that you're rounding out the words. you're not mumbling. So if you do those three things, you maximize comprehension. [music] What are the other two variables that change whereas these three are constant. The first is pauses. [music] So if I want to emphasize a point, what am I going to do? I'm going to pause. And the length of the pause will dictate whether you're just getting someone to draw attention or you're expecting a response. The second, your frequency on your voice. Basically, does your voice go up or does it go down? If we want to have your voice go up, what would we do in normal writing? We would put a question mark. Which means I could have a single word with a question mark behind it. I might say John. By saying that, I dictate that I am asking a question and I'm soliciting a response from the person. If I said John, I'm clearly not asking for a response right
source: 2025-11-24_lkWIdDdc3uc_5 Things To Get People To Buy
title: 5 Things To Get People To Buy

id: transcript::2025-11-27_eFHvstiWUQA_This Sales Guy Crushed All Records..::0000
text: We had a new sales guy who came in and crushed all of the records that had ever been done on that sales team. And there was a very experienced sales team. And I was like, what is this guy doing? Does he have higher close rates on the phone? And he didn't have higher close rates, but for some reason, he was able to get 30 to 50% more sales than everybody else. I was like, okay, so how is he getting more opportunities? And so we got on the call, we listened to all the all the scripts. We're like, he's not doing anything different. And so we pulled the guy up. We're like, dude, what are you doing? And he said, I don't know. Um, after I close the customer, I just say, who else do you know who might also want this? And I usually get like one out of three people to send me one or two other people. And I just do that on every sale cuz I learned that in my last job. And when he said that, it was like this big obvious duh that I'm sure was in the SOP at some point for the sales team. And of course, people get lazy because they don't want to scare the sale away. But by simply saying, hey, who else? Very clear. Who else do you know? Not do you know anybody? Yes. No. Who do you think would benefit from this? Who you'd want to do this with? Right? Because now you're actually asking them to solve a problem with their brain. Not make a quick yes no answer, which is what most people are just going to say, "No, I don't know anybody. Let's move on.
source: 2025-11-27_eFHvstiWUQA_This Sales Guy Crushed All Records..
title: This Sales Guy Crushed All Records..

id: transcript::2025-11-28_xy3eGxR8lEo_Dont Answer These Questions In A Sale::0000
text: This is a trap question. Hey, how many certifications do your trainers have? It's basically a blind question where whatever you say in response, prospect gets to be the judge of whether or not they accept that and then they choose to buy or not. And you don't know what the right answer is. And so rather than answer the question, you ask a question about the question. Which certifications are you looking for specifically? Now, if the person's like, do they have NASMAN ACE certifications? Now, if I don't have that for my trainer specifically, I would then say, why those certifications specifically? Right? Okay. And then they would say, "Well, I I I heard that they're good." It's like, "Well, those are amazing certifications. I agree with them. I'm not disagreeing. We have a couple other ones, and I'll tell you why we chose these rather than those." Now, if I just said, "Uh, our guys don't have that or they have this," I might have lost the sale right there. id: transcript::2026-01-05_UGIYp9W7-IE_My 5 Rules For Sales::0000
text: I have over 100 plus sales people who work for me across our portfolio that does over $250 million a year. These are five rules for closing that I teach them. Number one, the person asking the question is always in control and you want that to be you. Number two, be like smoke. If you don't know how to answer it, just ask a question about their question. Number three, tell them what their question means. They [music] might say, "I need to think about it." And you might say, "That's amazing. That's what some of our best customers have asked. What's your main concern?" And so instead of taking a step back, they actually take a step forward in the sale. Rule number four, use straw men for harsh truth. If you have a hard truth that you want to ask or a question that can seem kind of cutting, you don't want to ask it to them. You want to tell them a story of someone just like them that you ask the question to and then you have a third party in the sale who can then be the person you deliver the hard truth to and then they just bear witness. Five, [music] retain childlike curiosity at all times. And so if you say, "Huh, that's interesting." Or, "Huh, that's a really good question." That then keeps you in the sale. It keeps [music] rapport.

text: You train sales people through like role playing until your eyes bleed. Number one is you have to memorize a script. And by the time you blacked out every single word, you've said the script for as many times as there are words in the script, and you tend to know it. id: transcript::2026-01-14_fcW2ncPMFXs_The Van Westendorp Pricing Model::0000
text: Two guys ran a research study to figure out how to get the perfect price for any product. And they did it by asking four questions. And when getting those answers, they could plot them on a graph to find the perfect spot where you'd have the highest price with the most number of units sold, which is typically where you'll make the most profit. The first question you ask is at what price would this be so cheap that you wouldn't even believe this would work? And this honestly is where a lot of people who are beginners actually are. They price so low that no one actually thinks they could even deliver on the thing they're promising. The second question you ask is at what price would this be so high you wouldn't even consider buying it. This gives you the upper range for that particular customer. The next question you ask is at what price would this be a great deal? You believe it would work but it would be a bargain. And then fourth and last at what price do you think this would barely be in your range but you'd end up buying it anyways. And then this one tends to be the price point where you generate the most profit. And then by doing that, you can select a price, not by guesswork, but by data that'll make you the most
source: 2026-01-14_fcW2ncPMFXs_The Van Westendorp Pricing Model
title: The Van Westendorp Pricing Model

id: transcript::2026-02-03_7_NOrSBIYG0_We Make Our Landing Pages Like This::0000
text: Most landing pages suck. Here's how to have them suck less. First, start with the headline. You have to stop the person in their tracks and promise a clear outcome. That's it. Sub headline clarifies that promise. It's basically like in YouTube, you've got your headline and your thumbnail. It's the relationship between those two things. Add context to the headline. The hero image should add proof to the headline and sub headline. So, either I'm showing you the thing you're going to get or the outcome that you want to experience visually. The CTA should have what they're going to get and how they're going to get it, nothing else. For the form, you want to have as little information as required to get a qualified lead, but that could still be four or five pieces of information. In my experience, I tend to add more than I used to at the beginning cuz I used to want to get more opt-ins and now I want more customers. If you have more than five fields of information, break it into multiple steps. Optional, you can add oneline description to a lead magnet. The whole purpose is to answer why should I give my email? It's justification. If you're going to have bullets underneath of the fold, I like three bullets and it should be the three biggest objections in order of most comment to least common. Over time, I used to put a lot of social proof on my landing pages, but if for some reason I need it or it's a more complex thing, I will put social proof underneath. In terms of everything else visually, the point is to keep it blank because we want to direct all the attention towards doing the only thing you have to do. Often times, the more you lengthen the landing page, the lower it will convert. So keep it mobile optimized, keep it fast, compress all the images so it loads quickly. And then last but not least, put all the legal stuff so you don't get in trouble. And fundamentally the razor use for everything is if it doesn't increase optin percentage of qualified leads, cut
source: 2026-02-03_7_NOrSBIYG0_We Make Our Landing Pages Like This

text: And what are your choices if someone puts a gun to your head? >> What are you talking about? You do what they say or they shoot you >> wrong. You take the gun or you pull out a bigger one or you call their bluff or you do any one of 146 other things. There's two types of problem solving in life. There's convergent which is what they teach you at school. There's lots of variables and there's one correct answer and there's divergent thinking which is that there's many correct answers to a single problem. Most of life is divergent solutions not convergent solutions. So, for example, if I said, "How many uses of a brick can you think of?" Somebody who has a convergent process would only say, "Uh, bricks only build buildings." But somebody who has a divergent thinking process would think, "Okay, well, I could use as a doors stop. I could use it as a paper weight. I could spray paint it gold and make it a trophy. I could drill holes into it and use it as a potted plant and put some dirt inside of it. source: 2026-02-08_ir3ATIsg0VM_The 2 Types Of Problem-Solving

id: transcript::2026-02-09_BOFU4yMod9I_Does Raising Capital Make Sense::0000
text: Every business incurs debt at the beginning. You incur financial debt, talent debt, management debt, technical debt, data debt. There is always debt. Financial debt is actually usually one of the easier ones to do when you have a business that is profitable. Which is why so many of these massive companies start by saying, "Okay, well, we can make sure that all these other debts are not incurred so that we can have one quantifiable debt, which is money." So they raise capital. And then as a result, they're like, I can get the best talent. I can invest in infrastructure. I can price this not to maximize profit short-term, but instead to gain market share. Um, and I know that with economies of scale, for example, I'll be able to drive my profitability later. id: transcript::2026-02-20_cPjPTXT-KWc_My Complete Sales Framework::0000
text: How to structure your sales calls like the top 1% sales teams using the closer framework. So C is clarify. Clarify why the person is there. Label them with a problem. So that's label their current state, their desired state, and the gap that's stopping them from getting where they want to go. We want to position ourselves as the bridge that'll take them from where they are to where they want to go. Oh, overview their past pain. You overview past pain and experiences that they have tried before. You associate with what they liked about their past solutions and then disassociate with the things that they hated. Then go back to the top and ask what else and repeat this. It's called the pain cycle. S is sell the vacation. Come up with what I call a three-pillar pitch. For example, when I sold fitness, it was fitness, nutrition, accountability. Those are the three pillars. When I created a script to sell leads to realtors, it was do you want the leads to be timely, you want them to be exclusive, and you want them to be qualified. There's always three that you can chunk up or chunk down to. E explaining where their concerns. So people either blame circumstances outside other people, or avoid making the decisions themselves altogether. So, here's where they're going to bring up objections, and we want to answer them and then close the sale. Finally, and I added this years after teaching the close framework for a long time, is the R, which is reinforce the decision. Now, to be clear, this isn't selling your way out of a sale. Close the deal once they say yes. After it's closed, this is the handoff between the sale and when they begin. And all you have to do in this stage is make it clear what next steps will look like. And then keep your promises of making sure that those exact things happen when you said they would. So, people are like, man, these guys are on top of it. That's the closer framework. That's the overarching structure for top 1% sales teams.

title: My Complete Sales Framework

id: transcript::2026-02-22_9kE7IRyi0u8_This Is How I Manage My Time::0000
text: $250 million in revenue. That's what my portfolio did last year. And this is how I manage my time. Step one, define productivity. So productivity is the dollar output divided by hours input, dollars per hour. And so if your busy week didn't move one of those numbers, you weren't productive. Step two, determine if you're a maker, a manager, or both. So if you need two to four uninterrupted hours to produce your best work, you're a maker. If you can work in five to 60 minute chunks and still win, you're a manager. Depending on the season that you're in in business, you might need to switch between the two. Step three, plan your calendar. For a manager, a meeting costs you one full unit, so 15 to 60 minutes. You may have 20 plus slots per day, and an empty slot feels like wasted ROI. For a maker, which is usually what I am, most makers have two real blocks per day, so one meeting can steal 10% of your entire week. If you're both, you can do your first half your day as a maker and your second half your day as a manager. I did this for years. Or you can do one day as a manager schedule with a full day of meetings or every other day as a maker schedule with two working slots. Step four, teach your team the rules and then have them actually implement and respect them. If you're a manager, follow these steps. If you're a maker, follow these steps.
source: 2026-02-22_9kE7IRyi0u8_This Is How I Manage My Time

id: transcript::2026-03-03_vtJHzKRK5BY_How to Get Rich::0000
text: The first rule of money is spend less than you make. You don't need to listen to anything else. You don't need to do any investing, nothing else. The first rule of money is spend less than you make. The second rule of money is take what's left over and invested in making more money. I think the big piece, especially people who are starting out miss out is that they expect that they're going to get rich as rich people get richer. And it's a different strategy. When you're starting out, you have to think about how you're going to make money while you're awake, not while you're asleep. The only reason that people who are really rich think about how to make money while they're asleep is because they've already maxed out their waking hours. They can't put more time into investments. They have to, by consequence, pick passive things to make money. But they already maxed out their active. Currently, you haven't maxed out your active. And the returns on active are significantly higher and lower risk than passive income opportunities.

id: transcript::2026-03-04_MRVr8T4saSk_Just Do More::0000
text: What presents as volatility is typically a symptom of low volume. So if you're like, man, I only get like, you know, a sale every week or every other week. Most days I don't get a sale and then every once in a while I get one, it only appears volatile because you're doing so little per day. But if I looked at your year and saw that you closed, let's say, 12 customers in that year, you closed one a month, for example, every 3 or 4 weeks you get a customer. All I would do is look at your entire advertising activity for the year and say, "Okay, if we wanted to get 12 customers a day, we would have to do 365 times more advertising than we currently do." And if we did that on a daily basis, we would get 12 customers a day. And so, you just take your total calendar horizontally and then you flip it vertically for a day and that is how much volume is required. And so, most people just think that it's like, "Oh, they're they can't be doing more than like twice as much as me." But in my experience, the people who are crushing it literally are doing a thousand times more than
source: 2026-03-04_MRVr8T4saSk_Just Do More

id: transcript::2026-03-04_vb3gAtKUE1M_How To Get Good Employees To Stay::0000
text: I own a pest control company. We're $50 million this year. How do I get it to a billion dollars? We're not retaining any average talent, if that makes any sense. And so our A players are quickly rapidly rising to the ranks. We end up promoting them. They end up running a branch or whatever. >> And next thing you know, you you don't have any average average talent. Instead of it being like, oh, I I'm in I'm not an idiot, so I got promoted and I'm better than not being an idiot and I got promoted again. That's it. And now I'm going to leave because there's no other there's no career advancement for me, right? That's probably one of the reasons the literally the reason they'll sight on the way out, right? >> Yeah. >> Okay. So, we just need to create career advancement. The way that I like to think about career ladders and this applies to roles that are repeated within organization. So, this is sales, this is video editors, whatever. You've got title and you've got pay. I have junior normal and then senior for each role. The first thing you're going to do is you're going to go from junior to junior that's paid more. And then you're going to go to we're not going to call you junior anymore. And they're like, "Thank God." And that comes with a perk, which is that you don't have to work on Saturday nights. Then from there, we're going to go to here with a little pay bump. Then we're going to say, "Great. After you get your pay bump, you're now a senior." And then here we have our senior plus. But all of this could be the first title that you had. And then you repeat this at title 2. You repeat it at title three. They're always 3 to 6 months away from another promotion. There's always career advancement that exists. So just give them more ways to win.
source: 2026-03-04_vb3gAtKUE1M_How To Get Good Employees To Stay
title: How To Get Good Employees To Stay?
